title: Netflix customers targeted in phishing, tech support scam
description: The Better Business Bureau is warning Netflix customers about a scam. Con artists claiming they work for the video streaming service are trying to get money and private information from unsuspecting victims. Jericka Duncan reports.

asr.full_text: Canadian computer expert Jerome Segura investigations online scams. The latest has con artists targeting users of the popular video streaming service Netflix. It's a text report scam. Netflix customers get an email or pop-up ad directing them to a real looking but fake Netflix log-in page. Segura set up computer stripped of personal information and recorded the screen as he investigated the scam. After logging into the fake site, he received a notice. We have temporarily suspended this username. The page gave a 18000 number to call for support. Segura called the number and a con artist posing as Netflix tech support answered. The scammer said he could fix the problem, but first needed remote access to Segura's computer. The Scammer directed Segura on how to give him remote control. What you're seeing is the con artist actually downloading files off the computer. I had to set up fake banking spreadsheets on the desktop and they were taken as we were speaking. You want me to take a photo of the card? When the Scammer asked for credit card information, Segura ended the call. It was time for me to just hang up. The fake Netflix website Segura logged onto has since been taken down. Netflix told us, they believe the scam is no longer active, but Segura warns con artists could try it again, posing as other companies. Jerika Duncan, CBS News, New York.

textual.observation: The report describes messages directing Netflix customers to a realistic-looking fake Netflix login page, where users may be prompted to enter login information.

evidence.quote: Netflix customers get an email or pop-up ad directing them to a real looking but fake Netflix log-in page.
Con artists claiming they work for the video streaming service are trying to get money and private information from unsuspecting victims.

textual.context: Presented as a news report about a BBB warning and an investigation; the source attributes the claimed Netflix affiliation to the alleged actors rather than endorsing it.
textual.potential_relevance: The combination of a claimed Netflix-related destination and a request implied by directing customers to a fake login page describes a phishing mechanism requiring later context assessment.
textual.limitations: These records do not establish how many users received the messages, what information ordinary users entered, or whether the page remains accessible.

textual.observation: The described support-call scenario involved a caller posing as Netflix tech support, offering to fix a stated account problem in exchange for remote computer access and later requesting credit card information.

evidence.quote: The page gave a 18000 number to call for support.
The scammer said he could fix the problem, but first needed remote access to Segura's computer.
When the Scammer asked for credit card information, Segura ended the call.

textual.context: The source presents this as an investigator's recorded test of the reported scheme, not as an offer to viewers; the caller is described by the report as posing as Netflix tech support.
textual.potential_relevance: A claimed support identity is linked to a promised fix and requests for remote access and payment-card information, a concretely described mechanism requiring later context assessment.
textual.limitations: The records describe the investigator's test setup and do not establish that any ordinary customer granted access or suffered financial loss.

visual.observation: A Netflix-branded page shows a 'Member Sign In' panel with fields labeled 'Email' and 'PASSWORD,' a checked 'Remember me on this computer' option, and a blue 'Continue' button.
visual.context: Shown within a CBS News segment; frame F0018 labels the computer view as 'Segura Recording.' The surrounding report context appears to be demonstrative or journalistic rather than a direct viewer instruction.
visual.potential_relevance: The visible Netflix branding is linked to a request for account credentials, making it a candidate cue for review when evaluating demonstrated credential-entry flows.
visual.limitations: The sampled frames do not establish whether the page is official or unofficial, whether credentials were entered, what URL is loaded, or what occurred before or after the sign-in screen.

visual.observation: A Netflix-branded red screen displays an 'Important Notice' stating unusual activity was detected, the username has been temporarily suspended, and instructs the user to contact 'Member Services' at a partially obscured 1-800 phone number; it also shows an error code.
visual.context: Shown with CBS News watermark during a news segment. The screen presents itself as a Netflix account notice, but the report context is observational or demonstrative.
visual.potential_relevance: The claimed account suspension and unusual-activity warning are linked to a requested contact action via phone number, which is a concrete account-support flow candidate for review.
visual.limitations: The frames do not verify the phone number, the source of the screen, whether anyone called it, or whether the account notice is genuine.

visual.observation: A computer screen labeled 'Segura Recording' shows command-prompt style windows and a text editor with network-style output including lines such as 'IP address' and other system/network-looking information.
visual.context: Displayed in a CBS News report segment as recorded computer activity. The exact purpose of the commands is not fully legible from the samples.
visual.potential_relevance: The visible recorded computer activity follows earlier frames showing credential and account-support prompts, making it a candidate technical-demonstration cue associated with the reported flow.
visual.limitations: The sampled frames do not establish what commands were run, who ran them, whether access was authorized, or whether any data was exfiltrated or altered.

annotation.contextual_rationale: This video is non-scam content because it is a CBS News warning and investigation concerning reported phishing and fraudulent support interactions involving Netflix customers. The sign-in flow and requests for remote access and card information are attributed to a tested caller and presented as part of the investigation, not as instructions or an offer from the video. The report also qualifies the activity's current status and does not establish that customers granted access or lost money.
annotation.fine_grained_rationale: The primary subject is a warning and investigation of a reported third-party phishing and fraudulent support flow, including an investigator's recorded test, rather than an offer or instruction from the creator.
